title: Refund Handling for Window Contracts
content:
# Refund Handling for Window Contracts

Billing office note for Window Replacement Contracts.

**Rule.** A refund returns money from one specific earlier payment and is never larger than what remains unrefunded of that payment. Refunds go back by the tender rule: to the card or bank account a card or ACH payment came from, and by mailed check for a check payment; lender funding is never refunded to the customer and is instead returned to the lender by the financing account's terms. A payment that has already been refunded in full is never refunded again. A non-cooling-off refund is issued within the refund window counted in business days from the date it becomes due.

The tender rule is the series refund route (to the original tender) and the refund window is the series refund window in business days.

## Where a refund goes

| Source payment tender | Refund route |
|---|---|
| Card | Back to that card |
| ACH | Back to that bank account |
| Check | Mailed check |
| Lender funding | Never to the customer; returned to the lender under the financing account's terms |

## Limits per source payment

- A refund names one source payment and is never larger than what remains unrefunded of it.
- A payment already refunded in full is never refunded again; the payment's own refund records decide this.

## Hypothetical case

A hypothetical $1,000 card payment that already carries a $400 refund can be refunded by at most a further $600, back to that card; once $1,000 in total has been refunded against it, it is never refunded again.
